$comment: Deep-link targets per UPI app, used to bypass the contested `upi://` scheme.
JSON rather than TypeScript so build-time tooling can read the same table the
app code does. Expo config plugins, for one, are plain CommonJS running at
prebuild with no transpiler, and they need this to generate
LSApplicationQueriesSchemes (iOS) and <queries> (Android) -- a second,
hand-maintained copy of the list would drift.
These values are conventions observed across Indian merchant SDKs, not a
published spec, and apps change them between releases. `confidence` records
whether the deep link has been confirmed on a real device; `unverified`
entries are plausible but untested, and are excluded from getUpiAppTargets
unless explicitly asked for. See docs/verify-upi-targets.md for how to
promote one.
Coverage here is much narrower than the handle map in src/apps.ts, and the
gap is not an oversight. A handle is published data; a deep-link target has
to be tested. Detecting an app wrongly is cosmetic. Sending a payer into a
link that silently drops the amount is a failed payment.
`source` records where an unverified value came from. Play Store URLs are
self-proving -- the `id=` parameter is the package name -- and are the only
source used for Android packages here. There is no equivalent for iOS
schemes: they are published nowhere, and the third-party lists that collect
them have been wrong about apps in this very table, so no iOS scheme is
added without a device confirming it.
An entry with only an androidPackage is normal and useful: the Android
branch of buildUpiAppLink works from it, while iOS callers fall through to
the QR. Nothing here appears in getUpiAppTargets until it is `established`.
